findings.title: animate=True/'window' with continuous (per-observation) hue silently loses the animation: full trajectory drawn statically, window/trails never shown
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(2)
c = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(200, 6), axis=0)
ha = hyp.plot(c, animate='window', duration=4, frame_rate=10, focused=1, hue=np.arange(200.0), show=False)
ax = ha.figure.axes[0]
print(len(ax.lines))  # 0 -- animated window artists removed
print([len(getattr(a, '_segments3d', [])) for a in ax.collections])  # [39] full trajectory
ha.animation._func(30, *ha.animation._args)
print([len(getattr(a, '_segments3d', [])) for a in ax.collections])  # still 39 full segments
ha.save('hue_window.gif')  # every frame shows the whole rainbow trajectory
findings.expected: The 1-second opaque window slides along the trajectory (11 of 40 interpolated points visible per frame), colored by the hue gradient; nothing outside the window drawn.
findings.actual:
window_frames: 10
lines fargs: ['Line3D']
collection: Line3DCollection nsegs: 39
after frame30 collection nsegs: 39
(ax.lines empty; extracted gif frames f010 and f030 both show the ENTIRE rainbow trajectory, camera rotation only)
animate=True + continuous hue: ax.lines=0

findings.title: animate + legend + any trail flag (chemtrails/precog/bullettime) triples the canvas width; plot squashed into the left third
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(2)
b1 = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(150, 8), axis=0)
b2 = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(150, 8), axis=0)
ha = hyp.plot([b1, b2], animate=True, duration=2, frame_rate=5, chemtrails=True, legend=['groupA', 'groupB'], show=False)
print(ha.figure.get_size_inches())  # [19.2 4.8] -- 3x cap
ha2 = hyp.plot([b1, b2], animate=True, duration=2, frame_rate=5, legend=['groupA', 'groupB'], show=False)
print(ha2.figure.get_size_inches())  # [7.48975 4.8] -- correct without trails
findings.expected: Figure widened just enough for the legend (about 7.5in, as in the no-trail case); plot centered with the legend beside it.
findings.actual:
{'chemtrails': True} -> fig inches: [19.2  4.8]
{} -> fig inches: [7.48975 4.8    ]
{'bullettime': True} -> fig inches: [19.2  4.8]
{'precog': True} -> fig inches: [19.2  4.8]
fig tightbbox x1 (in): 7.33975 (on the 19.2in canvas); saved gif dims (3840, 960)

findings.title: Multi-dataset animations: frame count driven ONLY by the first dataset -- later datasets that are longer are silently truncated (67% never shown in a 3:1 case)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(2)
b1 = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(300, 8), axis=0)
b2 = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(100, 8), axis=0)
ha = hyp.plot([b2, b1], animate=True, duration=4, frame_rate=10, show=False)
print(ha.animation._save_count)                      # 40
print([d.shape[0] for d in ha.animation._args[0]])   # [40, 121] -- only first 40 of 121 ever rendered
findings.expected: The animation covers every dataset's full trajectory (e.g. frames = max over datasets, or a documented truncation warning).
findings.actual:
order [100,300]: frames = 40 | interp lengths = [40, 121]
-> longer dataset has 121 interp pts but only 40 frames are shown: fraction shown = 0.33
(order [300,100]: interpolated lengths [40, 14]; final pts per line: [21, 0] -- shorter dataset vanishes for the last two-thirds of the animation)

findings.title: Frame count off by one vs the docstring's 'exactly frame_rate * duration frames' (901/41 instead of 900/40 for some N)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np
for N, fr, dur in [(300, 30, 30), (10, 10, 4), (50, 10, 4), (300, 10, 4)]:
    iv = fr * dur / (N - 1)
    print(N, fr, dur, np.arange(0, N - 1, 1 / iv).size, 'target', fr * dur)
# hypertools-level: hyp.plot(np.cumsum(np.random.randn(300,10),axis=0), animate=True, show=False).animation._save_count == 901
findings.expected: Exactly frame_rate * duration frames for every N (900, 40, 40, 40).
findings.actual:
N=300 fr=30 dur=30: arange size=901 target=900
N=10 fr=10 dur=4: arange size=41 target=40
N=50 fr=10 dur=4: arange size=41 target=40
N=300 fr=10 dur=4: arange size=40 target=40

findings.title: Marker-only animations (fmt without a line, e.g. '.') ignore duration/frame_rate pacing: frames = raw row count
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(1)
walk = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(300, 10), axis=0)
ha = hyp.plot(walk, '.', animate=True, duration=4, frame_rate=10, show=False)
print(ha.animation._save_count)  # 300, not 40 -> saved gif plays 30s, not 4s
findings.expected: 40 frames (4 s at 10 fps), or a documented exception for marker-only animations.

findings.repro:

findings.title: GIF exports at the default frame_rate=30 play ~10% fast (27.0s for a requested 30s): 33ms delay rounds to GIF's 30ms centisecond grid
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from PIL import Image, ImageSequence
w = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(300, 10), axis=0)
ha = hyp.plot(w, animate='window', duration=1, frame_rate=30, focused=0.2, show=False)
ha.save('/tmp/d1fr30.gif')
im = Image.open('/tmp/d1fr30.gif')
durs = [f.info.get('duration') for f in ImageSequence.Iterator(im)]
print(len(durs), durs[0], sum(durs) / 1000.0)  # 30 frames, 30ms, 0.9s
findings.actual:
[E] window_d1_fr30.gif: n_frames=30, per-frame ms=[30, 30, 30], wall-clock=0.900s
trajectory.gif (spin, defaults): n_frames= 900  per-frame ms= 30  wall-clock s= 27.0
